ordinary_core_tower_and_standard_model_c.exact_model_return: A normal whole-pair isomorphism alpha pulls A_j, every original cup and partial row back to a genuine generating ordinary tunnel of M over N. No represented infinite reflection or trace substitution is assumed.
ordinary_core_tower_and_standard_model_c.ordinary_model_choice: 17.9 supplies compatible normal comparisons for every ordinary core with its recovered downward trace. The physical upward opposite trace remains distinct.
ordinary_core_tower_and_standard_model_c.represented_copy_boundary: The controlled-unitary model51.7–51.8 is strongly amenable as an abstract pair, yet for nonscalar v it is not an embedded core of the fixed larger ambient inclusion.
ordinary_core_tower_and_standard_model_c.human_source: Sorin Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II, Acta Mathematica172(1994), model definition1.4.1 printed186; Theorem4.1.2(i)–(v) printed210; Theorem5.1.1 printed226

extremal_opposite_model_characterization.ambient_scope: The whole physical opposite pair is B1=M1 prime cap T subset B0=M prime cap T with its inherited trace. Extremality is required for the universal characterization; finite depth is not. The reverse implication itself forces separable predual.
extremal_opposite_model_characterization.basis_transport: b_r=beta(a_r*) and support beta(f_r) return the right partial row after multiplication reversal; all Gram identities, fractional supports, row resolutions and scalar index remain.
extremal_opposite_model_characterization.noncircular_comparison: CTS.7 supplies rho from the entire ordinary core pair to the actual physical opposite pair under extremality, without assuming strong amenability and even before factorality of the core is known.
extremal_opposite_model_characterization.full_reverse: The supplied normal anti-isomorphism beta:M to B0 followed by rho inverse:B0 to R is a normal trace-preserving whole-pair isomorphism M to R. Two multiplication reversals restore ordinary multiplication.17.16 then supplies original strong amenability.
extremal_opposite_model_characterization.full_forward: 17.16 supplies an ordinary whole-model isomorphism alpha; rho alpha is the physical opposite-pair anti-isomorphism.17.17 gives the opposite pair a genuine ordinary generating tunnel.
extremal_opposite_model_characterization.retained_corrections: The index-ten original/opposite minimal trace multisets in63.9 exclude a universal unmarked characterization without extremality. The positive special nonextremal map62.6 and the separate represented-copy embedded-core obstruction51.7–51.8 remain at their exact scope.

amenability_and_model_interfaces.finite_families: POR.1–POR.21 and POR.5: under the original representation-amenability hypothesis, the complete unrestricted full finite family, marked corner return and entire residual, with original physical targets, both traces and all supported rows.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.forward_generation: SA.3–SA.7: canonical representation for any core; original strong-amenability finite-prefix approximation and proper/separable ordinary generation.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.full_compatible_state_return: 61.13–61.16: every smooth representation extends normally down the actual tunnel; uniform physical L2 return gives the full compatible possibly singular hypertrace and original strong-amenability/generating equivalence.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.nonseparable_global_equivalence: 61.17–61.20: original global finite approximation, relative amenability to an ergodic actual core and strong amenability are equivalent without ambient separability.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.ordinary_model_and_classification: 17.8–17.16: recovered downward trace, entire ordinary standard model, proper strongly amenable classification at arbitrary depth, real amplifications, full internal core towers and the ordinary-model converse.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.physical_opposite_model: 17.17–17.18: full normal anti-tunnel/core transport and both extremal physical opposite-model directions;63.6–63.13 supplies the actual inherited-trace opposite tower and canonical positive-cone traces.
amenability_and_model_interfaces.exact_negative_comparisons: CTS.7 gives the specified-reflection extremality criterion.63.9 refutes a universal unmarked comparison without extremality.51.7–51.8 refutes the bare represented-copy embedded-core assertion. AH/AB/AO and the fixed finite-kernel boundaries retain their exact negative scopes.

commutant_expected_tower.full_corner: PH.9: the actual opposite full corner gives a normal isomorphism of the commutant with the corner commutant, including arbitrary centers and an explicit finite inverse.
commutant_expected_tower.expected_tower: PH.10: every actual commutant step is a normal faithful smooth nondegenerate expected representation with the original supported basis and index; the entire next actual commutant is its expected basic construction with the original cup and dual expectation.
commutant_expected_tower.physical_trace: PH.11: the positive invertible density k=c^(-1)t, its finite frame bounds, the physical trace expectation sandwich formula and its original-stage expectation equal to1.
commutant_expected_tower.compatible_state: Under actual generation, the exact61.15 theorem applies to this smooth representation and supplies the compatible possibly singular M-hypertrace.
commutant_expected_tower.exercises: Two complete solved exercises distinguish faithful restriction from a nonfaithful larger compression and prove unitality of the physical trace correction.
commutant_expected_tower.hypotheses: Original finite-index II1 Jones tower with inherited physical trace; no extremality, finite depth or factorality of the opposite/commutant algebras. Actual generation is required only for the cited hypertrace consequence.
commutant_expected_tower.remaining_question: The full general nonextremal physical bicommutant D0=M remains open here. Fixed-step density bounds are not asserted uniform under arbitrarily many compositions.

physical_return_density_martingale.composed_densities: PH.12: the actual finite expected returns have pairwise commuting positive invertible density products, normalized conditional expectations and exactly the original-stage marginals.
physical_return_density_martingale.central_limit: PH.13: the martingale has a bounded limit h in the smaller commutant center,0<=h<=1. Its lost mass is exactly1-tau(h), and the state-distance limit is2(1-tau(h)).
physical_return_density_martingale.normal_minorant: PH.14: h E_U^tau<=E_N^tau on the entire positive cone of the original physical T. Positive spectral pieces of h are atomic; on each such atom the actual normalized factor-corner expectation gives index<=p_i/a_i. The total mass is at most the sum of squared atom traces; diffuse opposite centers give h=0.
physical_return_density_martingale.endpoint: PH.15: preserved unit mass, uniform integrability, constant density products and the full physical bicommutant are equivalent. No claim that the original generating/strongly amenable hypotheses force the unit mass is made.
physical_return_density_martingale.examples: Three complete solved exercises give the exact state distance, numerical atomic mass/index bounds and the independent bounded-increment probability diagnostic.
physical_return_density_martingale.hypotheses: Original finite-index II1 Jones tower and actual physical commutant expected representationPH.9–PH.11, with arbitrary opposite/commutant centers. No extremality, finite depth, core factoriality or amenability is needed for the structural theorems.
physical_return_density_martingale.remaining_question: The unrestricted original global-approximation/strong-amenability bicommutant implication requires exclusion of h=0. PH.22–PH.24 proves the full structural zero-one law,including faithful noninvertible limits;it does not exclude the zero branch at those original hypotheses.
physical_return_density_martingale.terminology: h is the central martingale limit and gives a normal minorant; no maximal normal component of an arbitrary extension state is asserted.
physical_return_density_martingale.credit: Independent exposition, proofs, solved exercises and diagram by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), CC0-1.0. model_and_physical_return_scope.model_characterizations: Theorems17.8–17.18: entire ordinary model and internal tunnel reconstruction at arbitrary depth, the full proper/separable ordinary-model converse, normal anti-transport, and the proper/extremal/separable physical opposite-model characterization.
model_and_physical_return_scope.model_traces: 63.6–63.13 identifies the whole actual tracial opposite tower and canonical positive-cone trace with arbitrary centers. Its universal unmarked nonextremal identification with the original pair is false63.9; the specified normal reflection has the exact extremality criterionCTS.7.
model_and_physical_return_scope.represented_cores: 51.7–51.8 gives the actual counterexample and exact correction for the represented-copy embedded-core assertion. The positive ordinary whole-model theorem concerns its specified normal map and actual pair.
model_and_physical_return_scope.physical_commutant_tower: PH.9–PH.11: actual normal faithful smooth expected tower with original supported bases, full next-stage construction and physical trace correction.
model_and_physical_return_scope.composed_physical_return: PH.12–PH.15: commuting normalized return densities, bounded central limit h, exact lost mass/state distance and a normal minorant with finite-index atomic support. The bicommutant endpoint is preserved unit mass; that conclusion under the original hypotheses is still open.

physical_return_sharp_index_mass.central_order: PH.16: t E_U^tau<=cp E_N^tau exactly when0<=t<=t_*,where t_*=sum_i(p_i/d_i)z_i,p_i=tau(z_i),d_i=[U z_i:N z_i]. The diffuse part and infinite-index atoms have coefficient zero.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.full_supported_return: PH.17: complete-positive order on the original physical T lifts through the entire finite supported-basis reconstruction of every actual return Phi_l,at all matrix sizes; the converse uses normal positive Kaplansky approximation.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.exact_limit: PH.18: h=t_* exactly,tau(h)=sum_i p_i^2/d_i,and lim_l||K_l-1||_1=2(1-sum_i p_i^2/d_i). Finite-index atomic corners have strictly positive limiting mass.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.factorial_gap: When U is a factor with r=[U:N],h=1/r. A proper factor inclusion has r>=2,so the limiting state distance is at least one. Infinite index gives distance two.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.examples: Three complete solved exercises distinguish positive from completely positive order,compute exact atomic mass and state distance,and explain infinite-index atoms and the factorial gap.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.hypotheses: Original finite-index II1 Jones tower and actual physical commutant expected representation PH.9–PH.15,with arbitrary commutant centers. Structural formulas use neither extremality nor amenability.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.remaining_question: The unrestricted original global-approximation/strong-amenability bicommutant implication requires exclusion of h=0. PH.22–PH.24 proves the full structural zero-one law,including faithful noninvertible limits;it does not exclude the zero branch at those original hypotheses.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.terminology: The sharp coefficient is maximal in the specified central family t E_U^tau. No maximal normal component of an arbitrary extension state is asserted.
physical_return_sharp_index_mass.credit: Independent exposition,proofs,solved exercises and diagram by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI),CC0-1.0. physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.shifted_amenability: PH.19: original global finite relative-commutant approximation passes to every upward shifted inclusion with its entire finite-prefix and finite-set scope,without ambient separability.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.finite_normality: If h>=epsilon1>0,the explicit p_i-normalized factor bases give a finite whole right M_j-row in every actual D_j. The existing sharp factor-index bound makes every state extending tau_Mj normal. M_j-centrality then makes it a trace.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.uniform_bound: The actual two-step center trace transport63.42 preserves the two finite sets of physical atom weights. These give a common bound on all central hypertrace densities c_j,not on the return products K_j.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.physical_trace_limit: PH.20: original dual cup identities descend compatibility through every earlier return. Every ultraweak cluster point of the bounded c_j commutes with the entire original tower and is normalized in the factorT,hence equals one. All physical returns preserve tau,and h=1,U=N,D_0=M.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.factorial_exclusion: PH.21: at the original global approximation hypotheses and with factorial U,the only index alternatives are one and infinite. The exact state-distance alternatives are zero and two. Every proper finite-index physical extension is excluded.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.remaining_question: The unrestricted original global-approximation/strong-amenability bicommutant implication requires exclusion of h=0. PH.22–PH.24 proves the full structural zero-one law,including faithful noninvertible limits;it does not exclude the zero branch at those original hypotheses.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.examples: Three complete solved exercises prove normality from the positive bound,compute the correct uniform central density,and distinguish finite-index exclusion from construction of an infinite-index counterexample.
physical_return_finite_index_exclusion.hypotheses: Original global finite approximation,strong amenability or a generating ordinary tunnel,with physical traces and actual expected commutant tower. The finite-index conclusion additionally assumes h bounded below; no extremality,finite depth or ambient separability is imposed.

Mathematical context: Popa,Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,§§3.1,4.1.2 and4.5.1. Exact existing dimension,finite-index,amenability and center-transport proofs are linked at their use.

physical_return_zero_one_law.common_support: PH.22: every shifted physical return limit H_j has the same support projection. It lies in every actual center and hence is scalar in the factorT: all limits are zero, or all are faithful.
physical_return_zero_one_law.reciprocal_traces: On the faithful branch, the central affiliated reciprocal densities define compatible normal semifinite traces Theta_j=tau(H_j^-1 .) on the entire positive cone. Infinite total trace is retained without normalization.
physical_return_zero_one_law.actual_center_transport: PH.23: the original full cup corner gives the exact center map two steps apart. The unital original factor and the actual Markov cup factor prove preservation of the physical trace. Dual expectation and bounded central truncations prove preservation of reciprocal trace weights. Surviving masses are two-periodic, including infinitely many atoms.
physical_return_zero_one_law.positive_mass_increment: PH.24: m_j-m_j-1=tau(H_j-1(k_j-1)^2 k_j^-1)>=0. Two-periodicity makes every increment zero; faithful spectral cuts force k_j=1 without a lower spectral bound.
physical_return_zero_one_law.structural_conclusion: The actual limit is h=0 or h=1, and the limiting state distance is zero or two. One finite-index atomic corner at any shifted stage forces U=N and D_j=M_j at every stage. Partial positive survival is impossible.
physical_return_zero_one_law.hypotheses: Original finite-index II1 tower and its actual physical commutant return. No amenability, extremality, finite depth, ambient separability or positive lower bound for h is imposed on the structural law.
physical_return_zero_one_law.remaining_question: The original unrestricted global-approximation/strong-amenability bicommutant implication still requires exclusion of h=0, or an exact counterexample satisfying every original hypothesis. The structural alternative does not decide that branch.
physical_return_zero_one_law.examples: Three complete solved exercises compute a strict positive mass increment, exclude the hypothetical17/54 atomic data from actual physical returns, and explain a faithful noninvertible abstract density with infinite reciprocal trace.
physical_return_zero_one_law.credit: Independent exposition, proofs, solved exercises and diagram by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), CC0-1.0. Mathematical context: Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,§§1.4.3 and4.5.1. The exact existing corner, Markov factor and finite return proofs are linked at their use.

physical_bilateral_cup_shift.proof_scope: PH.25–PH.28, equationsPH.85–PH.103, three exercises with full solutions.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.finite_maps: The original half-cup basis gives onto normal full matrix-corner maps with physical trace lambda times the diagonal sum. Fractional supports are retained. The induced relative-commutant maps agree under both index inclusions.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.normal_shift: The compatible maps and their inverses define one normal physical trace-preserving automorphism of the entire relative-commutant envelope. It moves every ordinary relative commutant and cup forward by two and is mixing.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.bilateral_commutant: The exact lower-cup corner return and two physical half-cup factor trace identities preserve the approximation error. Mixing proves that the commutant of every bilateral cup in the envelope is scalar;the envelope is a factor.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.generating_specialization: For an original generating tunnel, every integer core stage equals its physical ordinary stage and the envelope is the entire physical completion. The automorphism transports original stages, actual commutants, expected returns and physical density limits forward by two.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.hypotheses: An ordinary finite-index proper II1 inclusion with its actual physical trace. No extremality, finite depth, ambient separability or factoriality of an individual core is required for the envelope theorem.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.remaining_question: The original unrestricted strong-amenability/global-approximation bicommutant implication still requires exclusion of the zero-return branch h=0. Forward covariance and the scalar bilateral cup commutant do not establish that exclusion.
physical_bilateral_cup_shift.credit: Independent exposition, full finite-corner proof, solved exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), CC0-1.0. Source context:Sorin Popa, Some properties of the symmetric enveloping algebra of a subfactor, with applications to amenability and property T, Documenta Mathematica4(1999), Theorem4.10(a), pp.695–697.

physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.proof_scope: PH.29–PH.31, equations PH.104–PH.116, complete solved exercises PH.20–PH.22.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.hypotheses: Finite positive-character weighted balanced-word interval algebras, with their actual physical trace and a factorial left balanced completion. The phase vectors and original character are retained. Repeated labels and distinct marks with identical endpoints are permitted.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.entropy: The whole left center is the completed marked endpoint tail of the inverse walk. Factoriality gives sublinear endpoint entropy. Inversion and q^n=beta*p^(n-1)*alpha transfer the bound to both original phases and their inverse laws.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.mixing: The complete internal AB.4 proof gives all four marked tails. An exact finite-word posterior identity proves both left and right total-variation mixing, with the original asymmetric probabilities and no assumed reverse-mixing input.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.whole_commutants: Full prefix and suffix matrix fields give every finite commutant. Normal physical expectations at both ends give P_c-prime cap T_G=Q_c+1 and Q_s-prime cap T_G=P_s-1, so each physical half equals its entire bicommutant.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.ordinary_tower: The weighted pair vector has identity charge, scalar physical end expectation and the entire full cup corner. The existing Markov-factor basis and normal standard-form recognition give an actual ordinary Jones tower of index d=AB, with a generating lower tunnel and the same full tracial completion.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.conclusion: The actual return densities and limits equal one for this entire group-model class. Subexponential word-ball growth supplies factoriality automatically, including every finitely generated Abelian group and every positive character.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.remaining_question: The unrestricted non-group physical bicommutant and fixed-WM invariant endpoint remain open. The actual weighted-group class requires factorial left balanced completion. BFQ.3–BFQ.4 gives the separate affine counterexample to unrestricted common-support BF and scalar multiplicity;the bare second central local form remains open.
physical_weighted_group_bicommutants.credit: Independent exposition, proofs, exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), CC0-1.0. Mathematical context: Kaimanovich, The Poisson formula for groups with hyperbolic properties, Annals of Mathematics 152 (2000), sections 4–5, through the complete internal AB.4 proof; Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II, sections 1.4 and 4.5.

local_to_global_interfaces.supported_partitions: POR.1–POR.21 and Corollary POR.5: entire residual,each marked row,every prescribed prefix,with separate actual continuations for the cells.
local_to_global_interfaces.global_approximation: 61.13–61.20: full global finite-approximation equivalence;generating equivalence with the original ergodic-core hypothesis and separable predual.
local_to_global_interfaces.ordinary_and_opposite_models: 17.8–17.18: whole ordinary models and arbitrary-depth reconstruction;extremal physical opposite-model characterization.63.9 and51.7–51.8 give the distinct nonextremal pair and embedded-core corrections.
local_to_global_interfaces.local_approximation: 74.3–74.4: unequal-support first local form and every-core converse. BFQ.3–BFQ.4: actual affine counterexample to unrestricted common-support BF/constant multiplicity,also in the both-infinite-capacity regime. The bare second central local form remains open.
local_to_global_interfaces.physical_bicommutant: PH.22–PH.31: zero-one return law and the entire weighted-group class with factorial left balanced completion.The unrestricted non-group zero branch remains open.
local_to_global_interfaces.fixed_weighted_model: The original fixed-WM invariant zero-cost endpoint or exact positive all-state floor remains open,at the unchanged parameter,group,phase laws and physical traces.

scalar_central_multiplicity.proof_scope: IRG.1–IRG.3, equations IRG.1–IRG.14, complete solved exercises IRG.1–IRG.3.
scalar_central_multiplicity.indicator_rigidity: For an actual central indicator the weighted stationarity and joint defects have exact comparable positive integral formulas. The near-indicator bound retains the original lower transfer weight and costs 2(d+1) times the L1 profile error.
scalar_central_multiplicity.affine_obstruction: For matrix deletions of one fixed actual AH index-ten core, all finite projection states restrict compatibly to the same old canonical algebra. Every physical Folner net has joint defect lower limit at least3/5 and normalized distance to any one-level profile at least3/110. A finite physical test set obstructs every positive scalar central multiplicity; a finite approximate-profile bound is3/440.
scalar_central_multiplicity.quantifiers: IRG fixes the actual affine core before finite targets and allows all matrix deletions. BFQ.1–BFQ.4 supplies the return from a freely selected ordinary tunnel to one fixed core and excludes unrestricted BF and scalar-multiplicity rounding. Both affine unit capacities are infinite.
scalar_central_multiplicity.remaining_question: The bare second central local form,the unrestricted physical bicommutant and the original fixed-WM invariant endpoint remain open. The fixed-WM parameter,full group,phase laws and physical traces are unchanged.
scalar_central_multiplicity.credit: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI),CC0-1.0. Human context:Popa,Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,Theorem4.2.2,printed213–214. Full internal affine construction and separator:AH/AB/AO.

bounded_frame_quantifiers.central_profile: For a support qf with q in a unital cup-tail factor and f commuting with it,the normalized center trace equals tau(q)T_S(f). A relative L2 support error eta gives relative L1 profile error eta squared,uniformly at arbitrarily small support trace.
bounded_frame_quantifiers.fixed_core_return: Compatible finite ordinary-tunnel maps preserve the core pair and normalized center-valued traces. Actual returned projections in one fixed canonical algebra have the unchanged physical targets and nearly scalar profiles. No ambient map fixing M or infinite spatial conjugator is used.
bounded_frame_quantifiers.counterexample: The actual all-smooth-amenable affine index-ten inclusion has no unrestricted BF,even when the tunnel is selected after the finite physical targets. IRG.13 supplies the incompatible3/110 profile lower bound. Positive real scalar multiplicity reduces to integer multiplicity through actual n^2 core deletion.
bounded_frame_quantifiers.valid_results: Conditional BF-to-local and rounded-projection-to-BF theorems,precise factorial-core specializations,variable integer rounding,unequal-support first local approximation,and the full finite supported partition retain their stated hypotheses.
bounded_frame_quantifiers.separate_question: The bare second central local form permits a general tail projection and remains open. The unrestricted physical bicommutant and the original fixed-WM invariant endpoint retain their original hypotheses and data.
bounded_frame_quantifiers.credit: Exposition,proofs,exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI),CC0-1.0. Scholarly context:Popa,Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,Theorem4.2.2 and Corollary4.2.3,printed213–215.

tail_projection_profiles.profile_range: For C=N_l intersection S,D=Z(C),a projection p in C and a projection f in B_l,the profiles T_S(qf) for projections q below p are exactly E_Z(f t),where t ranges over the central order interval0<=t<=T_C(p). Prescribed scalar traces restrict exactly tau(t).
tail_projection_profiles.finite_partitions: Every finite positive central partition of T_C(p) is realized by an orthogonal projection partition of p in the same C,including the full residual. Its supported products partition pf exactly.
tail_projection_profiles.concentration: The central support replacement error is at most tau(T_C(q)|f-z|),hence at most ||T_C(q)||infinity ||f-z||2 squared. Relative error carries concentration chi(q)=||T_C(q)||infinity/tau(q).
tail_projection_profiles.sharp_example: An explicit finite-factor diagonal inclusion has central commutant support,scalar T_S(q),relative support error tending to zero,and relative product-profile error two. Its concentration factor is exactly1/tau(q).
tail_projection_profiles.scope: The exact range and partition realization are at one fixed stage. Simultaneous physical commutator and compression estimates required by the bare second local form remain unresolved.
tail_projection_profiles.credit: Exposition,proofs,exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI),CC0-1.0. Scholarly context:Popa,Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,Theorem4.2.2 and Corollary4.2.3,printed213–215. Exact trace and projection prerequisites:TE16 and56.1.

cup_center_transfer.theorems: 68.6–68.8 and TP.5–TP.6;equations CT.1–CT.12 and TP.15–TP.23;four solved exercises.
cup_center_transfer.cup_transfer: The original cup satisfies d E_D(cup)=kappa. Its full corner transports the larger center to the internal two-step tail center,and expectation onto the smaller center is exactly Q_kappa.
cup_center_transfer.joint_trace: Simultaneously transporting both neighboring centers two steps preserves their joint inherited trace and gives a normal isomorphism of the actual joint centers.
cup_center_transfer.profile_ranges: At depth2n the whole-unit profile range is T^n([0,1] in Z(S));at depth2n+1 it is T^n Q_kappa([0,1] in Z(R)),where T=Q_kappa P0. The corresponding central order interval gives the complete range below any prescribed tail projection and all finite partitions,including the full residual.
cup_center_transfer.integrable_stability: For every nonzero positive integrable profile zeta,the realizing projection at prescribed depth l has normalized profile error at most ceil(l/2) times its relative stationarity defect,plus twice its relative L1 truncation error. Its physical trace can be arbitrarily small.
cup_center_transfer.scope: The ordinary tunnel and every prescribed prefix are fixed throughout. Realizing projections may depend on depth and cutoff. Their simultaneous physical commutator and compression estimates remain required for the bare second local form.
cup_center_transfer.credit: Exposition,proofs,exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI),CC0-1.0. Scholarly context:Popa,Classification of amenable subfactors of type II,Theorem4.2.2,printed213–214. Exact internal Jones and finite dual-trace constructions:17.14,63.1–63.4 and82.1–82.5.

tail_physical_moments.theorems: TP.7–TP.10; equations TP.24–TP.36; four solved exercises.
tail_physical_moments.moment_selection: In every finite type II algebra, a positive contraction below a prescribed projection has a projection with the same full center-valued trace and any prescribed finite family of normal scalar moments. No separability or factoriality is required.
tail_physical_moments.physical_coefficients: At one fixed original tail stage the projection retains every prescribed physical A_l-coefficient, the full supported central profile and the exact physical mass. The finite projection f in B_l need not be central. The ordinary tunnel and its entire earlier Jones prefix stay fixed.
tail_physical_moments.energy: The squared commutator error plus twice the squared compression error equals twice the physical support trace times the coefficient defect. This gives exact normalized bounds sqrt(2D) and sqrt(D).
tail_physical_moments.partition_boundary: The projection and its full complement retain all moments. Three explicit rank-one positive effects in Mat2 tensor a II1 factor have no orthogonal projection partition with all their individual matrix moments. The central-profile partition theorems remain valid.
tail_physical_moments.scope: The bare second local form still requires a positive contraction with simultaneously small physical coefficient defects and the appropriate finite support. Central-profile matching alone does not imply these bounds.
tail_physical_moments.credit: Exposition, proofs, exercises and figure by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), CC0-1.0. Scholarly context: Sorin Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II, Theorem 4.3.1, printed pp. 217–219. Center-valued trace and projection prescription: TE16 and Lemma 56.1.
